item.title: GloRilla Announces Big Glo’s 901 Turkey Drive In Memphis
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: GloRilla will give away Thanksgiving turkeys at Smackers in Memphis on November 24. Doors open at 3 p.m. Central.
item.content:encoded:
GloRilla is giving away Thanksgiving turkeys in Memphis on Tuesday (November 24).

The rapper announced Big Glo’s 901 Turkey Drive on Sunday, with doors set to open at 3 P.M. Central at Smackers, 569 South Highland Street. Turkeys will be available while supplies last.

“Tuesday 11/24 !!! Meet me there don’t beat me there,” GloRilla wrote in the announcement shared on Instagram and Facebook. Smackers operates several locations, and the restaurant’s own directory confirms the South Highland address.

The turkey drive comes less than two months after GloRilla surprised students at Cordova High School during homecoming.

She brought a $25,000 check for the school and told WREG’s Alex Coleman she had already been looking for a way to give back when a coach invited her to homecoming.

In December 2024, she brought another $25,000 check to her alma mater, Melrose High School. The donation was for renovating the library, which school officials said would bear her name and offer resources to students and the surrounding Orange Mound neighborhood.

“I try to make it my mission to do this every year,” GloRilla said in an interview with WREG. In 2023, she returned to Westside Middle School, where she once attended classes, and made a $20,000 donation.

The Westside gift was meant to give students a chance to take trips outside Memphis.

item.title: Jodeci Cancels Louisville Show After K-Ci Hailey Suffers Severe Dehydration
item.dc:creator: Houston Williams
item.description: Jodeci canceled its Louisville concert after K-Ci Hailey suffered severe dehydration.
item.content:encoded:
Jodeci canceled its Sunday (Nov. 22) concert at the Louisville Palace after K-Ci Hailey suffered severe dehydration and received immediate medical attention, tour representatives said in a statement shared with AllHipHop.

The R&B group was scheduled to perform in Louisville, Kentucky, as part of its tour celebrating the 35th anniversary of Forever My Lady.

The show was scheduled for 8 p.m., but fans learned shortly after 10:30 p.m. that it had been called off, Louisville Public Media reported. Concertgoer Macarra Hunter told the outlet she understood that a medical emergency had to take priority. What frustrated her was how long the audience waited for an explanation. She said she met fans who had traveled from as far away as Kansas and St. Louis. 

“K-Ci received immediate medical attention, and his health and well-being remain the top priority. He and the group sincerely apologize to their fans who came out to share the evening with them and understand the disappointment this unexpected cancellation may have caused.”

K-Ci also addressed fans in an Instagram video, thanking them for their support and apologizing to those who came out in Louisville. He said he was already in Memphis, where the tour team expects him to rejoin Jodeci for Tuesday’s (Nov. 24) show at the Orpheum Theatre. 

For Louisville ticket holders, the tour team said refunds will go back to the original payment method through Ticketmaster. Louisville Public Media reported that the refunds are automatic for purchases made through Ticketmaster and should appear within 14 to 21 days after the company receives the funds from the event organizer. If a ticket was transferred, the refund goes to the original purchaser. 

Hunter still found a little humor in the night. She told Louisville Public Media she played “I’m Still Waiting” all the way home. After two and a half hours at the Palace, she knew exactly which Jodeci song fit the ride

item.title: Havoc Hopes To Settle Mobb Deep Lawsuit With Prodigy’s Estate
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Havoc responds to Prodigy's estate over Mobb Deep's concert and merch money and says he wants to resolve it amicably.
item.content:encoded:
Havoc says he hopes to settle things amicably with Prodigy’s estate after it sued him over money from Mobb Deep shows and merchandise.

The Queens rapper addressed the dispute in a November 20 Instagram post, saying he welcomed a chance to tell his side.

“Now the truth gets to come out. still keeping them in my heart and pray we settle things amicably,” Havoc wrote.

The federal docket shows the case was filed October 30 in the Southern District of New York. Prodigy’s widow, Ikesha Dudley, brought the suit against Havoc and two of his companies.

As AllHipHop previously reported, Dudley says the estate owns half of Mobb Deep LLC but hasn’t received its share of live performance or merchandise earnings since Prodigy died in 2017.

She alleges the act played at least 172 concerts after his death, and that Havoc kept her from seeing the company’s books.

Dudley says the duo created Mobb Deep LLC in 2000 to manage its business and hold its trademarks and copyrights. In the account previously reported by AllHipHop, she alleges Havoc kept her out of management and routed Mobb Deep business through two companies he controlled.

The estate wants the companies to turn over their financial records and pay what it says it is owed.

It also wants Prodigy’s master recordings returned, putting control of the recordings in dispute alongside the money from shows and merchandise.

Dudley says the shows spanned North America, South America and Europe. She claims performance fees and merchandise sales brought in millions. The estate also seeks additional damages intended to punish the conduct it alleges.

The estate and Havoc had previously worked together on Infinite. Mass Appeal released the album in October 2025, pairing vocals Prodigy left behind with new production from Havoc and The Alchemist.

“I spoke to the estate about this album, and this album only. That’s where my focus is,” Havoc told the Recording Academy while discussing the unreleased material that went into the project.

Havoc’s post expressed a hope for a settlement, not an agreement with the estate.

The estate is asking for a jury trial.

item.title: Justin Timberlake’s Apple TV Trailer Revisits Janet Jackson’s Super Bowl
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Justin Timberlake's Apple TV trailer revisits the 2004 Super Bowl with Janet Jackson. The four-part series starts December 11.
item.content:encoded:
Justin Timberlake was already a Janet Jackson fan long before the two shared a Super Bowl stage. Apple TV’s first trailer for TIMBERLAKE shows him as a teenager pointing out a Jackson poster in his bedroom before it revisits an appearance that followed them both for years.

Apple confirmed that Fisher Stevens directed four episodes with new interviews and archival footage. The first two debut globally on December 11, the third follows on December 18 and the finale lands on December 23.

In the trailer, Timberlake says viewers will see “these incredibly sweet and goofy things from my childhood, and some things that are really hard to talk about,” according to People. The preview also touches on his time with *NSYNC, his relationship with Britney Spears and his 2024 arrest.

Jackson headlined the Super Bowl XXXVIII halftime show in Houston on February 1, 2004. Timberlake joined her as a surprise guest and pulled away part of her costume at the end of “Rock Your Body,” exposing her breast, as the FCC’s account documents.

A source told Variety, as AllHipHop previously reported, that Jackson would discuss the halftime show in the series. Apple’s trailer revisits the performance, but its announcement didn’t confirm a new interview with her.

Jackson spoke for herself in her 2022 A&E and Lifetime documentary. “Of course, it was an accident that should not have happened but everyone is looking for someone to blame and that’s got to stop,” she said, as Entertainment Weekly reported. Jackson said the two had moved on. She also said Timberlake asked her to join him at his 2018 Super Bowl show and she declined.

The trailer traces Timberlake’s shift from *NSYNC to a solo career and includes appearances by two producers who helped shape that sound: Pharrell Williams and Timbaland. The Recording Academy credits Pharrell Williams, Chad Hugo and Timbaland among the producers on Justified, which won the Grammy for Best Pop Vocal Album in 2004.

Timbaland went on to produce “SexyBack” with Nate “Danja” Hills on FutureSex/LoveSounds. “My Love,” Timberlake’s collaboration with T.I. from that same album, won Best Rap/Sung Collaboration in 2007.

item.title: Pray For 2 Chainz: Reportedly Crashed Cybertruck
item.dc:creator: illseed
item.description: 2 Chainz posted footage of a badly damaged orange Cybertruck on Instagram Stories, leaving questions about what caused the reported crash and whether anyone was hurt.
item.content:encoded:
We do not like seeing 2 Chainz on the ground with a CyberTruck all crashed up.

The ATL rapper put the aftermath of a reported crash on Instagram Stories, giving us a close look at a badly damaged orange Tesla Cybertruck.

The video appeared on his verified account, and the first few seconds tell you why people are asking what happened. The truck is sitting on grass at night, with visible damage around the front wheel. What appears to be a deployed side curtain airbag fills the window. This was a rough night! I mean, I am no fan of this truck, as some of you know. It looks like it was drawn with a ruler. 

Some reports say it was “totaled.” And it looks like it probably was. But, take a look and you tell me what you think.

https://www.instagram.com/p/DgGT4qQhlR-/?hl=en

The Cybertruck looks like it has an expensive appointment ahead of it, but we’ll see if it was total loss. They are set to stop these cars soon, so maybe he gets lucky?

READ ALSO: Elon Musk Puts Kibosh On Tesla Cybertruck

To be real, there are other questions. Who was driving? Where did it happen? Was anybody hurt? It was on 2 Chainz’s account, but we never saw him.

There’s a reason some of you might be getting déjà vu. Back in April, 2 Chainz shared a different Cybertruck video and said a woman tried to run him off the road. This was reportedly a near collision. He was also hospitalized after a separate crash during Art Basel in Miami in December 2023. Hmmmmm….

The latest IG Story gives us a much better view of the truck than it does of the circumstances. I hope he is OK. Last thing we need is something tragic or crazy happening. That’s reserved for the beginning of the new year.


Get better, TityBoy and get paid!

item.title: Trick Williams Says He Has A Music Project In The Works With Lil Yachty
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: WWE star Trick Williams says he's working on a music project with Lil Yachty after their "Gingerbread Man" collaboration.
item.content:encoded:
Lil Yachty and WWE wrestler Trick Williams turned a wrestling rivalry into a diss track this spring. Now Williams says he’s working on a whole music project with Yachty.

“Whole project on the way,” Williams said when asked about recording more with Yachty in an interview on Double Coverage.

Williams has released music under his own name and said he recorded it before he thought it could become a job.

“Rapping is something that I always did for fun. It was kind of like wrestling,” he said.

Their first song together came during Williams’ feud with Sami Zayn. They put out “Gingerbread Man” ahead of WrestleMania 42, turning their running joke about Zayn into a diss track.

The day after it dropped, they brought a life-size Gingerbread Man to SmackDown as part of the rivalry.

Yachty said he and Williams had met at a couple of shows before Williams messaged him and the two spent nearly two hours on the phone talking about working together.

They came up with the nickname for Zayn themselves.

“Just me and Trick clowning and calling him Gingerbread Man,” the rapper told Chris Van Vliet in a separate interview. He recalled spending time in his dressing room with Williams, coming up with jokes and figuring out how to use them on the show.

Williams beat Zayn for the United States championship at WrestleMania, with Yachty in his corner.

By September, Yachty was taking bumps himself: AllHipHop covered his WWE in-ring debut against Baron Corbin at Sunday Night’s Main Event.

Under the match’s stipulation, Yachty had to last five minutes against Corbin to earn Williams a shot at the title. He made it to the time limit, and Williams went on to win the championship later that night, according to WWE’s results.

Williams also talked on Double Coverage about training alongside Yachty.

item.title: Don Toliver Moves London O2 Show & Manchester Fans Get Refunds
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Don Toliver's O2 show moves to December 15, while Manchester ticket holders get automatic refunds after the evacuation.
item.content:encoded:
Don Toliver has moved his Monday, November 23 concert at The O2 in London to December 15 after his Manchester show was cut short. Tickets for the London show will carry over to the new date, while Manchester ticket holders will receive automatic full refunds.

“Due to production delays following last night’s show at Co-op Live in Manchester, tonight’s Don Toliver concert at The O2 is rescheduled to December 15,” a venue representative said in a statement reported by The Independent.

Toliver confirmed the December 15 date on Instagram Stories and expressed sympathy for fans who were hurt in Manchester. “I just wanna make sure everyone is safe and the next show goes on properly,” he wrote.

He said performing for fans was the only thing he loved more than making music.

The two London stops on the Nitrous tour were booked back-to-back. The other show remains listed for Tuesday, November 24 on OVO Arena Wembley’s official calendar. The venue lists doors at 6:30 P.M. local time.

The O2’s ticket policy says that if a buyer can’t attend a rescheduled event, the organizer decides whether to offer a refund. The ticket seller is supposed to contact the buyer with that policy.

As AllHipHop previously reported, police evacuated Co-op Live on Sunday, November 22, after people at the concert began feeling the effects of an unknown substance. Greater Manchester Police said venue staff alerted officers shortly after 10 P.M.

Police declared a major incident so emergency services could coordinate their response. More than 12,000 people were escorted out of the arena.

Medics assessed more than 80 people at the venue, according to updated figures from the North West Ambulance Service, as reported by The Associated Press.

Some reported eye or breathing symptoms. One person was taken to Manchester Royal Infirmary for further assessment, and the ambulance service carried out decontamination as a precaution.

Concertgoer Joey Howe told Sky News he watched people move toward the concourse and saw paramedics attending to fans there. The broadcaster published video coverage of the evacuation.

Police initially suspected tear gas, but their investigation into the substance was still ongoing Monday. Co-op Live said it was working with investigators to determine what happened.

item.title: Takeoff’s Accuser Asks To Permanently Drop Lawsuit Against His Estate
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: The woman who sued Takeoff in 2020 has asked a judge to permanently end her civil case against the rapper's mother and estate.
item.content:encoded:
Takeoff‘s accuser has asked a judge to permanently end her civil lawsuit against the Migos rapper’s mother and estate.

Her attorneys filed the request on November 17, MyNewsLA reported. They asked for a dismissal “with prejudice,” which would bar her from filing the same case again.

Five days earlier, lawyers on both sides had told Los Angeles County Superior Court Judge Huey P. Cotton they’d resolved the case.

As AllHipHop previously reported, Cotton turned the December 1 date reserved for jury selection into a hearing to check on the case.

Estate attorney Tamar Yeghiayan had told the judge, “A dismissal is forthcoming,” according to Rolling Stone’s account of the November 12 hearing. Neither side disclosed the terms at the time. MyNewsLA reported that the later dismissal request didn’t give a reason for dropping the case.

The woman sued under the name Jane Doe on August 5, 2020, opening Los Angeles Superior Court case 20STCV29465.

In the original complaint, she alleged Takeoff raped her at a house party in Encino that June and brought civil claims including sexual battery, assault and false imprisonment.

Takeoff denied the allegations through his lawyer, Drew Findling. Los Angeles prosecutors declined to file criminal charges in April 2021, citing insufficient evidence, but Doe’s civil suit continued.

Doe said in her original filing that she used a pseudonym “to protect her privacy.”

Takeoff was killed in Houston on November 1, 2022, at 28. His mother, Titiana Patrice Davenport, became the administrator of his estate in Georgia, and the California lawsuit went on after his death.

The estate had separately asked the court to end the case in October. Its attorneys said Doe deleted text messages they considered relevant, while her lawyers said the defense waited years to request them and never sent a notice asking her to preserve them.

The court didn’t resolve that dispute after Doe decided not to proceed to trial, MyNewsLA reported.

Doe’s original complaint asked for damages to be determined at trial, including punitive damages, along with attorney’s fees and costs.

Doe previously filed a separate $6 million creditor’s claim against the estate in Georgia.

item.title: EXCLUSIVE: Jagged Edge Frontman Replies To Woman’s Assault Allegations With Fiery Response
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Jagged Edge's Brandon Casey denies a woman's childhood sexual assault allegations. His lawyer says he plans to seek sanctions.
item.content:encoded:
Brandon Casey of Jagged Edge is denying a woman’s allegations that he sexually assaulted her as a child, and his lawyer says the defense intends to seek court penalties against her and her attorney.

Leron E. Rogers of Fox Rothschild LLP gave AllHipHop’s Grouchy Greg Watkins the statement on Casey’s behalf on November 23.

In the civil complaint, which AllHipHop first reported, Tyliyah S. Lee alleges Casey assaulted her five times in Philadelphia when she was between six and 10. Lee alleges she suffered emotional distress, depression and anxiety, and seeks more than $50,000 in compensatory and punitive damages on a single civil battery claim.

Rogers addressed those allegations directly: “Our client, Brandon Casey of Jagged Edge, flatly rejects the untrue allegations of battery and sexual assault set forth in the civil Complaint.”

Lee also alleges that she showed Casey a song she had written when they met at a community event in 2003 and that he took it without compensating her. Jagged Edge released “Walked Outta Heaven” that year on Hard; the label-supplied credits list Brandon Casey, Brian Casey and Bryan-Michael Cox as writers.

Rogers said the song is not the subject of a separate claim in the lawsuit.

“The Complaint also invokes the 2003 song ‘Walked Outta Heaven’ but asserts no claim of authorship or copyright infringement, and the song’s published credits do not include the Plaintiff,” Rogers told AllHipHop.com.

Lee filed the case in Philadelphia’s Court of Common Pleas in September.

In the November 19 filing that moved the case to federal court, Casey denied the allegations of wrongdoing and disputed that Lee was entitled to any recovery. U.S. District Judge Chad F. Kenney set December 18 as the deadline for Casey to respond to the complaint.

Rogers said the defense intends to seek sanctions, or court penalties.

“Mr. Casey will not be pressured by headlines, and he will not stand by while his name and reputation are attacked. We intend to pursue sanctions and every other available remedy against the Plaintiff and her counsel for bringing claims we believe have no basis in fact.”

Rogers added: “Mr. Casey believes genuine survivors of abuse deserve a voice and our full respect, and baseless claims only diminish their cause.” He said the defense would not comment further at this time.

Here is the full statement from Leron E. Rogers of Fox Rothschild LLP on behalf of Brandon Casey:

Our client, Brandon Casey of Jagged Edge, flatly rejects the untrue allegations of battery and sexual assault set forth in the civil Complaint. The claims stem from events alleged to have occurred some twenty years ago, are baseless & unsupported by any corroboration we are aware of and have already been met with a firm denial in court.

The Complaint also invokes the 2003 song “Walked Outta Heaven” but asserts no claim of authorship or copyright infringement, and the song’s published credits do not include the Plaintiff.

Mr. Casey will not be pressured by headlines, and he will not stand by while his name and reputation are attacked. We intend to pursue sanctions and every other available remedy against the Plaintiff and her counsel for bringing claims we believe have no basis in fact.

Mr. Casey believes genuine survivors of abuse deserve a voice and our full respect, and baseless claims only diminish their cause.

In deference to the court and the parties involved, we will have no further comment at this time.

item.title: Mike Jones Brings Thanksgiving Help To His Old Houston High School
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Mike Jones goes back to his old high school to put H-E-B turkey vouchers and grocery gift cards in Houston families' hands.
item.content:encoded:
Mike Jones went back to his old high school in Houston on Sunday (November 22) to help families pay for Thanksgiving dinner.

Hundreds of people drove through Nimitz High School to pick up H-E-B vouchers and gift cards, and Jones stopped to hug people and take photos as cars moved through the lot.

The rapper joined Houston City Controller Chris Hollins and the Gulf Coast Community Services Association for the giveaway. Volunteers handed drivers envelopes with a $20 voucher for a turkey or ham and a $50 gift card for other groceries, the Houston Chronicle reported.

For Jones, who attended Nimitz, the drive meant seeing people again on familiar ground.

“I got nostalgia just when I pulled in,” Jones told the Chronicle. “Just nostalgia to see the people still coming back to show the love.”

It was the first Thanksgiving drive the three partners put on together. Debra Fisher, the nonprofit’s interim CEO, told the Chronicle that 775 vouchers and gift cards were available, and that using them instead of handing out turkeys kept costs down and gave families more choice.

The line spilled out of the parking lot onto W.W. Thorne Drive. Houston grandmother Odalis Matute told the Chronicle she’d been unsure how to buy a turkey for the more than 10 relatives she expected at Thanksgiving, then spent about an hour in line.

The Gulf Coast Community Services Association lists a community food pantry and emergency assistance among its regular programs in the Houston area.
